title: Annotatio II §.VI: Ascelinus follows Paschasius on corporal presence, yet defends coexistence not conversion
pass_a_gloss: For Ascelinus, in a Letter to Berengar himself, edited by Dacherius from old membranes of the Abbey of Casale Benedicti, even if he confesses he follows Paschasius’s sentence (namely as far as the corporal presence of Christ’s flesh in the sacrament pertains), nonetheless writes far otherwise than he about consecrated bread and the mode of presence of Christ’s body in the Eucharist — defending not Conversion of bread into Christ’s Body, but at least Coexistence of the Body with the blessed bread.
pass_b_english: Ascelinus’s letter to Berengar (Dacherius, from Casale Benedicti membranes) owns Paschasius on corporal presence of Christ’s flesh in the sacrament.
On consecrated bread and the mode of presence he writes far otherwise: not conversion of bread into body, but at least coexistence of the Body with the blessed bread.
source_text: Ascelinus enim, in Epistola ad Berengarium ipsum, per Dacherium ex antiquis membranis Abbatiæ Casalis Benedicti, editâ, etiamsi confiteatur, se Paschasii sententiam sequi (nempe quantum ad corporalem carnis Christi praesentiam in sacramento attinet) tamen de pane consecrato & modo praesentiae corporis Christi in Eucharistia longè aliter, ac ille, scribit, non Conversionem panis in Corpus Christi, sed tamen ad minimum Coëxistentiam Corporis cum pane benedicto, defendens.

lemmas.gloss: coexistence of the Body with the bread
